prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator, and its experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: After reading the full set of opening ballots I move my preferred configuration from my own first choice, dynamical mean-field theory (B054), to the topological insulator ballot (B057). B057 is the only candidate that is ranked by seven of eight members, four of them in their top three, and it combines a clean, original theoretical idea (the Kane-Mele Z2 classification of spin-orbit-driven band insulators) with a decisive experiment (Molenkamp's HgTe quantum wells). Its interpretation is stable after more than fifteen years of independent confirmation in HgTe, InAs/GaSb and three-dimensional materials by photoemission, and it connects directly to first-principles electronic-structure work on real compounds, which is the part of it I can judge from my own field. A theory-plus-experiment trio is a natural prize structure. My loyalty to DMFT is real, but only Mehlig and I ranked it, and a broad base of support across subfields counts for something even though it is not a measure of merit.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed HgTe as the platform that made the experiment possible, and the three-dimensional generalisation (Fu, Kane, Mele; Moore and Balents; Hasan and Cava) is not represented in the credited names. Zhang's death removes one claimant from eligibility, but Bernevig and Hughes remain, and a three-person limit forces a choice that will be contested. There is also the thematic overlap with the 2016 prize on topological phases and phase transitions, and the optical lattice clock (B027) has the strongest opening support, with three first places and five top-three rankings, so a prize that does not honour it needs justification.

responses.point: Mehlig ranked B057 fifth and flagged that the credited trio omits the HgTe proposers Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (Zhang deceased), leaving a real allocation question, and he partly doubted whether DMFT, which he ranked sixth, is a physical discovery or a computational method.
responses.response: I agree the allocation is the real weakness of B057 and I do not think the supplied list resolves it fully. I would argue the citation can be framed around the Z2 classification and the observation of the quantum spin Hall state, which the Kane-Mele and Molenkamp credits cover, and which does not hinge on who first named HgTe. On DMFT, I accept the force of his distinction between a method and a phenomenon: the Mott transition and correlated-metal physics it describes are physical, but a prize for a framework is harder to cite than one for a discovery, and Metzner's omission from B054 compounds this. That is a main reason I now rank B057 above my own B054 as the preferred configuration.

responses.point: Danielsson ranked B057 second and called the idea original, clear and widely impactful, but raised the overlap with the 2016 prize and the contested credit among the HgTe proposal, the 3D discovery and the original Kane-Mele work.
responses.response: I share his view of the science. On the 2016 overlap I would draw a firm line: the 2016 prize rewarded topological phase transitions and the Thouless-Haldane-Kosterlitz framework, while the Z2 insulator with protected helical edge states is a distinct, later concept with a separate experimental discovery, so I do not see it as the same achievement. Where I would qualify his comfort is on credit: contested claims do not make the case weaker scientifically, but they do mean the committee should word the citation narrowly rather than claim the whole of topological materials.

responses.point: Lindroth ranked the optical lattice clock (B027) first and called it a clean atomic-physics case with a fair two-person credit, and ranked B057 second, calling it timely or even overdue relative to 2016.
responses.response: I take her argument for B027 seriously: Katori and Ye are a clean attribution, the performance is confirmed by many laboratories, and I cannot claim expertise in precision metrology to rank it against topological insulators on merit. Our disagreement is therefore about which I would place first, not whether B027 is deserving, which is why it is my first alternative. I would resist her description of B057 as 'overdue', because that is a statement about timing, not about whether Kane, Mele and Molenkamp are the right three. Her ballot does support my judgement that B057 is mature and stable.

responses.point: Pearce ranked IceCube (B041) first and B027 second, noting that B057 is original and timely but that a fair prize may be contested because of the omitted HgTe and 3D contributors, and he rated B014 as possibly premature because the origin of its superconductivity is unsettled.
responses.response: His point about credit for B057 is one I fully share, and I think it is the main thing the chair should expect in the discussion. I agree with his maturity concern about twisted bilayer graphene (B014), which I also ranked fourth for the same reason, and that consistency is part of why I favour the better settled B057. I cannot judge the IceCube attribution within a large collaboration from my field, and I would defer to him and Danielsson on whether Halzen and Karle are the decisive pair.

uncertainties: Whether the committee can accept a narrowly worded citation for Kane, Mele and Molenkamp given the omitted HgTe proposers and the 3D topological insulator contributors.
Whether the 2016 prize on topological phases is read as already covering this ground.
How B057 should be weighed against B027, which has stronger opening support but sits outside my expertise.
My recollection of the exact priority dates in the HgTe and 3D topological insulator literature is from memory and not verified here.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B057, B027 or B054. I note that B054 (DMFT and DFT+DMFT) and B057 (spin-orbit band topology) lie close to my own electronic-structure research, which is a topical proximity rather than a documented personal or institutional connection, and my profile lists no relationship with any credited person.
